How review and approval work

Work breadth first: approve one photo for every species before adding second photos, then repeat. Existing pilot photos are retained. The queue follows checklist taxonomy within each round. Filters narrow what you browse; they do not bypass the global round. Species with all candidates skipped are flagged as needing replacement candidates.

Read the linked eBird / Merlin account, paraphrase useful ID guidance, and inspect the actual Macaulay photo. Select up to two visible features. Click a feature’s “Place arrow” button, then click the photograph. Labels stay outside the photo in the preview. Keep explanations short; use general tips for fuller context.

Saving a draft does not publish it. Approval requires source and image checks and publishes both the photo callouts and general species tips. Editing an approved photo keeps its previous approved version live until you approve the changes. “Remove from quiz” withdraws its approved tips. Quiz histories and scores are unaffected by review work.

Source text belongs to eBird / Merlin, Cornell Lab of Ornithology. Our summaries and placements are experimental adaptations, not Cornell-reviewed or endorsed annotations. Do not infer a feature that is hidden in a photo. No screen capture is used by this workspace.
